In addition to the other information included in this annual report and the exhibits, you should also carefully consider the
following factors related to our ordinary shares and American Depositary Shares (" ADSs "). There may be additional risks that
we do not currently know of or that we currently deem immaterial based on information currently available to us. Although we
have a formal risk policy framework in place, the maintenance and development of which is undertaken on an ongoing basis so
as to help management address systematic categories of risk associated with our business operations, any of these risks could
have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations, leading to a decline in the trading
price of our ordinary shares or our ADSs. The risks described below may, in retrospect, turn out to be incomplete and therefore
may not be the only risks to which we are exposed. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we now
believe are immaterial (and have therefore not been included), could also adversely affect our business, results of operations or
financial condition. The order of presentation of the risk factors below does not indicate the likelihood of their occurrence or the
magnitude or the significance of the individual risks.
Summary of Risk Factors
Risks Related to Commodity Prices, Cash Flow and Financial Performance
1 Our profitability, cash flows, Mineral Reserve estimates and shareholder returns are highly dependent on
commodity prices
2 Foreign exchange volatility may materially affect margins, earnings and project returns
3 Inflationary pressures and escalating input costs may erode profitability and reduce future returns
4 Our future growth strategy depends on sustained cash generation, continued access to capital and our ability
to service our debt and comply with financial covenants
5 Certain factors may affect our ability to support the carrying value of our property, plant and equipment and
other assets, resulting in impairments
6 Our financial flexibility could be constrained by exchange control regulations in the jurisdictions in which we
operate
7 Sovereign, political, regulatory and macroeconomic developments in the jurisdictions in which we operate
may adversely affect our business
8 We are subject to mining taxes, royalties and other regulatory imposts, and to policies and legislation relating
to greater state intervention in the mining sector
Risks Related to Operations and Business Resilience
1 Safety incidents and loss of life may result in production losses, regulatory intervention and reputational
damage
2 Exposure to mining-related health hazards may result in occupational disease and significant long-term
liabilities and costs
3 Infectious disease outbreaks and endemic disease may disrupt our workforce and operations, and increase
costs
4 Production is dependent on reliable energy supply and increasing energy costs may materially affect
profitability
5 Water ingress, pumping obligations at adjacent closed mines, flooding and decant risk could interrupt
operations and create long-term liabilities
6 Infrastructure constraints and ageing infrastructure could adversely affect our operations
7 Illegal mining and organised criminal activity pose growing operational and safety risks
8 Disruptions in critical supply chains may affect production, project execution and profitability
9 Reliance on trackless mobile machinery ("TMM") exposes us to equipment-related production interruptions
10 The use of contractors may expose us to delays or suspensions in mining activities and increases in mining
costs

5 Intense industry competition and consolidation may adversely affect our ability to acquire assets, equipment
and skilled personnel
Risks Related to Climate, Environment and Social Licence
1 Climate change presents material physical risks to our operations and long-term value creation
2 Decarbonisation, carbon pricing and emerging climate regulation may increase costs and capital requirements
3 Environmental liabilities, rehabilitation obligations, biodiversity requirements and closure costs may be
materially higher than expected
4 We may have exposure to rehabilitate groundwater and land pollution, and financial provisioning requirements
may require additional provisions
5 Our operations depend on water use licences and other environmental authorisations
6 A tailings facility failure could have far-reaching consequences, and adverse developments concerning the
proposed deep-sea tailings placement ("DSTP") at Wafi-Golpu could materially adversely affect the project and
our business
7 Failure to maintain our social licence to operate could affect current and future operations
8 We may fail to meet environmental, social and governance ("ESG") performance expectations and published
targets, which could affect reputation, stakeholder confidence and access to capital
Risks Related to Technology, Cybersecurity and Digital Resilience
1 Technology failures could disrupt mining operations and business continuity
2 Cybersecurity incidents may materially disrupt operations and expose Harmony to financial and reputational
harm
3 Failures of our IT security processes and violations of data protection laws may result in regulatory penalties,
fines and reputational damage
4 Emerging technologies, including art ificial intelligence ("AI") , may introduce new operational, legal and
governance risks

4 Litigation, regulatory proceedings and other legal disputes may result in material losses and operational
